implementation_statement: Access control policy POL-02 and standards STD-02.1 to STD-02.4 (P06) apply to the PSGCS. STD-02.4 OT Access Standard adds OT-specific rules for shared operational accounts, console access, and vendor sessions.

OT accounts are requested through the OT access workflow, approved by the Vice President, Gas Control or the Director of Compression Engineering, and created in the OT domain from role templates. Account types: controller, senior controller, SCADA engineer, station operator, vendor (gateway only), and service. Gap: 3 of 60 sampled OT accounts of transferred staff were not removed within 5 business days, and PS-3 still uses local accounts on the legacy SCADA (POAM-008; POAM-016).
evidence: OT account register; P07 AC-2 results

implementation_statement: HR leaver and mover events trigger automatic disablement tickets for OT accounts; disablement in the OT domain is executed within 4 hours by the OT service desk. Gap: PS-3 legacy SCADA accounts are disabled manually from a weekly report until migration (POAM-016).
OT accounts inactive for 35 days are disabled by a scheduled job in the OT domain. Vendor gateway accounts are disabled after each approved session window.
Account creation, modification, enabling, disabling, and removal in the OT domain and on the gateway are logged and forwarded to the SIEM through the GCC-1 log collector.

The SCADA platform enforces area-of-responsibility and role permissions: controllers can command only the desks and pipeline segments assigned for the shift; engineers cannot issue control commands from engineering workstations.
evidence: SCADA role and area matrix approved 2026-02-10

implementation_statement: The DMZs at GCC-1 and GCC-2 enforce one-way flows from the historian to the DMZ replica and from the DMZ to cloud analytics. No business system can open a session into the SCADA network. Rules are reviewed quarterly against the documented communications baseline.
evidence: Firewall rule export; quarterly rule review

implementation_statement: SCADA display and database changes are built by SCADA engineers, verified point to point by a second engineer and field technician, and released only after a gas control supervisor approves. Engineers cannot approve their own changes.
evidence: Change workflow configuration; P07 CM-3 results

implementation_statement: Least privilege is built into OT role templates. Administrative rights on SCADA hosts and station HMIs are held only in privileged OT accounts checked out through OT privileged access management.
evidence: OT role templates; privileged access report

implementation_statement: Security functions (role assignment, audit settings, alarm configuration, firewall rules) are limited to named SCADA administrator and OT security roles.
Administrators use separate non-privileged accounts for routine work; privileged OT accounts have no email or internet access.
Use of privileged OT accounts is recorded by OT privileged access management with session video, and reviewed weekly by the OT monitoring cell.

Engineering workstations and the gateway lock an account after 5 failed attempts for 15 minutes. Controller consoles alert the SOC instead of locking, so a controller is never locked out during operations; this deviation is documented in the Cybersecurity Implementation Plan.
evidence: Domain policy export; console alert rule

implementation_statement: A system use notification is displayed at logon on SCADA consoles, engineering workstations, station HMIs where the platform allows, and the gateway.
Engineering workstations allow 2 concurrent sessions per user; gateway sessions are limited to 1 per vendor user.

Engineering workstations lock after 10 minutes. Controller consoles do not lock because controllers must see alarms at all times; physical access to the control room floor is the compensating control.
evidence: Domain policy export; CIP compensating control entry

implementation_statement: Gateway sessions terminate at the end of the approved window or after 30 minutes idle; engineering remote sessions terminate after 60 minutes idle.

control_name: Permitted Actions Without Identification or Authentication
implementation_statement: No action on the SCADA is permitted without identification except viewing the public-safety wallboard in the control room lobby, which shows no control functions.

All vendor and remote engineering access to the PSGCS is meant to pass through the OT remote access gateway with MFA, per-session approval, and session recording. Gap: 7 always-on cellular modems used by one compression manufacturer for turbine monitoring remain outside the gateway (POAM-004).
evidence: Gateway session report; architecture design review 2025-04; P07 AC-17 results

implementation_statement: The gateway and OT monitoring sensors record and alert on every remote session; the OT monitoring cell reviews unexpected sessions in real time.

control_name: Protection of Confidentiality and Integrity Using Encryption
implementation_statement: Remote sessions to the gateway use TLS 1.2 or higher; site-to-site tunnels for SCADA telecommunications use IPsec.
Remote access reaches the PSGCS only through the two gateway nodes in the GCC DMZs.

Wireless is prohibited inside the SCADA network at the GCCs. Licensed radio and microwave links in SYS-05 are point-to-point and encrypted where the radios support it. Wireless intrusion detection runs at both GCCs.
Mobile devices are not allowed on control room consoles. Field tablets reach station HMIs only through the station engineering port with an OT account, never through wireless.
External systems may not connect to the PSGCS except vendor laptops through the gateway or, on site, through a company-owned transient device. Personal devices are prohibited.

Sharing of PSGCS data with JV owners and interconnecting pipelines is limited to defined data sets agreed in operating and interconnect agreements, published through the shipper services platform, not from the SCADA network.
evidence: Data sharing schedule in operating agreements

implementation_statement: Not applicable: the PSGCS hosts no publicly accessible content. Public information about the pipeline is published on the corporate website, outside the boundary.
Awareness and training policy is part of POL-05 and STD-05.1 (P06).

All workforce complete annual awareness training, including phishing and insider threat; controllers, station operators, and OT engineers also complete an OT module covering removable media, transient devices, and reporting abnormal SCADA behavior.

Controllers train on cyber-caused abnormal operating conditions (loss of SCADA, false data, forced manual operation) in the simulator each year; OT engineers complete ICS security training every two years. Gap: PS-3 controllers have not yet completed the cyber AOC simulator module, and 6 of 25 sampled OT engineers were past due for ICS training (POAM-017).
evidence: Training records; simulator scenarios; P07 AT-3 results

implementation_statement: Training records are kept in the learning system for 5 years; operator qualification records follow the OQ program.
Audit and accountability requirements are set in STD-01.4 Audit Logging Standard (P06), including OT log sources and the 12-month retention period.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-02 Security operations (SOC and OT monitoring cell)
implementation_statement: Logged events include logons, privileged actions, control commands with user and console, alarm acknowledgments and inhibits, configuration downloads to controllers, firewall allows and denies, and gateway sessions. The OT monitoring cell reviews the event list annually.
evidence: STD-01.4 event list; SCADA event journal

implementation_statement: SCADA event records include time, console, user, point, old and new value, and outcome; firewall and gateway records include source, destination, and session ID.
Historians and log collectors at each GCC have storage for 18 months of events, with alerts at 80% use.

control_name: Response to Audit Logging Process Failures
implementation_statement: Log collection failures alert the OT monitoring cell; SCADA continues operating (logging failure never stops control).

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
provider_if_inherited: CCP-02 Security operations (SOC and OT monitoring cell)
implementation_statement: The OT monitoring cell reviews correlated OT events in the SIEM continuously, with daily review of privileged sessions and weekly review of firewall exceptions. Gap: logs from 22 compressor stations, including all 20 PS-3 stations, are kept locally and not forwarded, so they are reviewed only during investigations (POAM-006).
evidence: SOC review records; log source list; P07 AU-6 results

provider_if_inherited: CCP-02 Security operations (SOC and OT monitoring cell)
implementation_statement: Review, analysis, and reporting are automated in the SIEM with OT use cases tied to the communications baseline.

control_name: Audit Record Reduction and Report Generation
provider_if_inherited: CCP-02 Security operations (SOC and OT monitoring cell)
implementation_statement: The SIEM provides search and report generation for investigations without altering original records.
SCADA hosts, station PLCs where supported, and log collectors synchronize to GPS-disciplined time servers at each GCC.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-02 Security operations (SOC and OT monitoring cell)
implementation_statement: Forwarded logs are stored in a write-once archive; only the SOC platform team can manage retention, and SCADA administrators cannot delete forwarded logs.
Each control command is attributed to an individual controller login on the console; shared accounts are not used on GCC consoles.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-02 Security operations (SOC and OT monitoring cell)
implementation_statement: Logs are retained 12 months online and 3 years in the archive. Gap: 22 compressor stations keep logs locally for 90 days only (POAM-006).

Audit generation is enabled on SCADA hosts, consoles, historians, DMZ hosts, the gateway, and OT domain controllers. Gap: legacy station HMIs at 22 stations log locally with limited event types (POAM-006).
Privileged OT sessions are recorded as video by OT privileged access management and kept 12 months.
Assessment, authorization, and monitoring requirements are set in STD-01.2 (P06) and the TSA-approved Cybersecurity Assessment Plan.

Internal Audit, with a co-sourced OT assessment firm, assesses PSGCS controls each year so that at least one-third of Cybersecurity Implementation Plan measures are assessed each year and all within 3 years.
evidence: P07 plan and results; Cybersecurity Assessment Plan schedule

implementation_statement: Assessors are independent of the teams that design and operate the controls; the co-sourced firm signs an independence statement each year.
Interconnection security agreements cover the JV owners' data feeds, interconnecting pipelines' measurement links, and the cloud analytics feed. Each is reviewed every 2 years.
PSGCS weaknesses are tracked in the enterprise POA&M (P07) with owners and dates, and reported monthly to the executive risk committee.
The COO is the authorizing official equivalent and decides continued operation each year on the CISO's recommendation (SSP section 4.2).

provider_if_inherited: CCP-02 Security operations (SOC and OT monitoring cell)
implementation_statement: Continuous monitoring covers OT network monitoring alerts, configuration drift, patch status, and Cybersecurity Implementation Plan measure status, reported monthly.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-02 Security operations (SOC and OT monitoring cell)
implementation_statement: IT penetration testing runs annually; a purple team exercise against the IT/OT boundary ran in 2026-05 under rules of engagement that exclude live control functions.
evidence: Penetration test and purple team reports

implementation_statement: Internal connections between SCADA hosts, historians, consoles, and the telecommunications front end are documented in the PSGCS data flow register.
Configuration and change management requirements are set in STD-01.5 (P06), which incorporates management of change for control room operations (192.631(f)).

Hardened baselines exist for SCADA hosts, consoles, historians, engineering workstations, and station HMIs on PS-1 and PS-2. Gap: PS-3 baselines are incomplete, and legacy HMIs at 22 stations cannot meet the baseline (POAM-003; POAM-016).

SCADA, station control, and firewall changes go through management of change with a gas control representative, testing in the SCADA test environment, and point-to-point verification before release. Gap: 2 of 40 sampled display changes lacked point-to-point verification records (POAM-009).

control_name: Automated Documentation, Notification, and Prohibition of Changes
implementation_statement: The change workflow documents proposed changes, requires approvals, blocks unapproved releases, and notifies the control room before release.
Security and safety impact analysis is part of each change record, including alarm and display impact on controllers.
Only SCADA administrators using privileged OT accounts through OT privileged access can change production; logic downloads to station PLCs require the station key switch in program mode.

control_name: Automated Access Enforcement and Audit Records
implementation_statement: Access restrictions on production changes are enforced and logged automatically; downloads outside approved change windows alert the OT monitoring cell.

Configuration settings follow the hardened baselines and the SCADA vendor's security guide. Gap: 22 legacy stations deviate (unsupported operating systems, default services) under documented exceptions (POAM-003).
Unneeded services, ports, and protocols are disabled on SCADA hosts and consoles; only protocols in the communications baseline cross zone boundaries.
Application allowlisting runs on SCADA hosts and consoles at both GCCs. Planned: allowlisting on station HMIs as they are replaced (2027 to 2028).

The OT asset inventory covers hardware, software, and firmware for SYS-01 and SYS-03 to SYS-05 and is reconciled monthly with passive discovery. Gap: 7 of 60 sampled PS-3 field devices were missing from the inventory (POAM-015).
evidence: OT asset inventory; P07 CM-8 results

implementation_statement: Inventory updates are part of every installation, removal, and change record.
The configuration management plan for the PSGCS defines roles, configuration items, and the SCADA test environment.
Software is used under license; the SCADA vendor license and maintenance agreement is tracked by the software asset team.
Users cannot install software on SCADA hosts, consoles, or engineering workstations; allowlisting blocks it at the GCCs.
The location of PSGCS information (SCADA databases, historians, configuration backups, SSI and CEII documents) is recorded in the data location register.
Contingency planning is set in STD-03.3 (P06) and integrated with the O&M manual and emergency plans (192.605, 192.615).

The PSGCS contingency plan covers loss of GCC-1 (failover to GCC-2), loss of telecommunications, and manual operation. Gap: it does not address a failure or compromise of the SCADA platform that affects both GCCs, or PS-3 recovery beyond manual operation (POAM-011; POAM-016).
evidence: PSGCS contingency plan v6; P07 CP-2 results

implementation_statement: The plan is coordinated with the emergency plans, the Cybersecurity Incident Response Plan, and the compressor station local operation procedures.
Controllers and station operators train on failover and manual operation each year.

GCC-1 to GCC-2 failover is tested each calendar year at intervals not exceeding 15 months (last 2026-04-22). Gap: PS-3 manual operation has not been drilled at scale since the acquisition, and GCC-2 isolation has not been exercised (POAM-012).
evidence: Failover test report; P07 CP-4 results

implementation_statement: SCADA backups are copied to an offline store at the other GCC each week.
GCC-2 is a hot standby for PS-1, PS-2, and JV pipelines. Gap: PS-3 has no alternate control site until migration (POAM-016).
SCADA telecommunications use microwave, two MPLS carriers, and satellite backup at stations. Gap: PS-3 has a single carrier and 140 meter and valve sites are cellular-only (POAM-021).

SCADA databases, configurations, and PLC logic are backed up daily to the GCC backup server and weekly to offline media; backups are scanned for malicious code when made and before restore. Gap: PS-3 SCADA backups are kept online in PS3-CR with no offline copy (POAM-016).
evidence: Backup log; scan records; P07 CP-9 results

implementation_statement: Backups are restored to the SCADA test environment each quarter to test reliability and integrity.
Recovery and rebuild procedures exist for SCADA hosts and consoles at both GCCs. Gap: no tested rebuild procedure for the PS-3 legacy SCADA (POAM-016).
Identification and authentication requirements are set in STD-02.2 and STD-02.4 (P06), including the memorized secret reset schedule required by SD 02G Section III.C.1.a.

Users of SCADA consoles, engineering workstations, and the gateway are uniquely identified. Gap: shared operator accounts remain on station HMIs at 31 stations (permitted as critical for operations under SD 02G Section III.C.4, with compensating controls), and PS-3 uses local accounts (POAM-001; POAM-016).
evidence: OT account register; shared account register

implementation_statement: Privileged OT access requires MFA through OT privileged access management with hardware tokens.

MFA is required for remote and engineering access. Control room consoles at GCC-1 and GCC-2 use compensating controls documented in the Cybersecurity Implementation Plan (badge-controlled control room, console bound to controller role, session logging). Gap: PS3-CR lacks the badge-controlled floor and console logging (POAM-016).
Field devices are identified by address and certificate where supported; the SCADA front end rejects unknown device addresses and the OT sensors alert on new devices.
Identifiers are assigned on approval and never reused; vendor identifiers are tied to named individuals.

Memorized secrets are reset on the STD-02.4 schedule (365 days for user accounts, 180 days for privileged and shared accounts) and on departure of anyone who knew a shared password. Gap: 4 of 25 sampled departures did not trigger a shared password change, and mitigations for 14 components that cannot be reset are past their timeline (POAM-001; POAM-007).
evidence: Password age report; shared account register; P07 IA-5 results

implementation_statement: OT passwords are at least 15 characters, checked against a breached password list, and stored hashed.
Authenticator feedback is obscured on all PSGCS logon screens.
Cryptographic modules in the gateway, VPN concentrators, and domain controllers use validated algorithms configured by the vendor security guides.
Vendor users (non-organizational users) are identified individually on the gateway, sponsored by an internal owner, and use MFA.
Users must re-authenticate when privileges change, when a gateway session window ends, and after 12 hours on engineering workstations.
Identity proofing occurs at hire through HR verification; vendor identity is verified by the sponsoring owner and the vendor's employer attestation.
Incident response is set in POL-03 and STD-03.1 to STD-03.3 (P06); the Cybersecurity Incident Response Plan is maintained as required by SD 02G Section III.F.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-02 Security operations (SOC and OT monitoring cell)
implementation_statement: Responders, controllers, and OT engineers named by position in the plan receive role-based incident training each year.

The plan is exercised each year, testing at least two of the objectives in SD 02G Section III.F.1.a to III.F.1.d with the named positions taking part (2026-03-18: containment and IT/OT isolation at GCC-1). Gap: isolation at GCC-2 and PS3-CR has not been exercised (POAM-012).

provider_if_inherited: CCP-02 Security operations (SOC and OT monitoring cell)
implementation_statement: Incident handling covers detection, containment, segregation of infected devices, memory capture, eradication, and recovery, with OT steps owned by the Director of OT Security and gas control decisions owned by the Vice President, Gas Control. Gap: 3 of 25 sampled incidents had hosts reimaged without a memory image (POAM-024), and PS-3 incidents are handled with separate legacy tools (POAM-016).

provider_if_inherited: CCP-02 Security operations (SOC and OT monitoring cell)
implementation_statement: Incident handling uses security orchestration playbooks that define, prioritize, and drive standardized response steps.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-02 Security operations (SOC and OT monitoring cell)
implementation_statement: Incidents are tracked in the case management system with timelines, decisions, and reporting clocks.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-02 Security operations (SOC and OT monitoring cell)
implementation_statement: Cybersecurity incidents are reported to CISA as soon as practicable and no later than 72 hours after identification (SD 01G Section II.C); the Director of OT Security is the primary Cybersecurity Coordinator.
evidence: Report records; coordinator roster filed with TSA

provider_if_inherited: CCP-02 Security operations (SOC and OT monitoring cell)
implementation_statement: An incident response retainer with OT experience and the SCADA vendor's emergency support are available 24x7.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-02 Security operations (SOC and OT monitoring cell)
implementation_statement: The Cybersecurity Incident Response Plan names positions and resources and covers containment, segregation, backup integrity, and IT/OT isolation governance. Gap: the SEC materiality step does not yet include curtailment and shutdown factors, and the disclosure committee has not exercised an OT shutdown scenario (POAM-013).
Maintenance requirements are set in STD-01.6 (P06).
Maintenance of SCADA hosts, station controls, and field devices is scheduled and recorded in the work management system.
Maintenance tools and transient devices are company-owned, registered, and scanned at a kiosk before connecting to OT.
Nonlocal maintenance must use the gateway with approval, MFA, and recording. Gap: 7 always-on vendor modems remain at compressor stations (POAM-004).
Vendor technicians on site are escorted by a qualified employee and use company transient devices.
Spare parts for SCADA hosts, station PLCs, and RTUs are stocked at regional warehouses with defined replacement times.
Media protection is set in STD-04.2 (P06), including SSI and CEII handling.
Access to backup media, configuration exports, and SSI documents is restricted to named roles.
SSI and CEII records must be marked under 49 CFR 1520.13 and the CEII procedure. Gap: 3 of 25 sampled TSA submission records were unmarked (POAM-010).
Offline backup media are stored in locked cabinets at the other GCC.
Backup media are moved between GCCs by employees in locked cases with a custody log.
Media from OT systems are sanitized or destroyed by a certified vendor with certificates kept.
USB ports on consoles and HMIs at the GCCs are disabled; removable media are allowed only through the scanning kiosk.
Physical security is set in STD-01.7 (P06).
Access authorizations for control rooms and equipment rooms are approved by the Vice President, Gas Control and reviewed quarterly.

GCC-1 and GCC-2 control rooms use badge plus PIN at controlled entries with guards 24x7; compressor stations use fences, badge readers on control buildings, and video. PS3-CR uses badge only (POAM-016 adds the controlled floor).
evidence: Badge logs; video retention report; P07 PE-3 results

implementation_statement: Telecommunications rooms and cable paths at the GCCs are locked and monitored.
Control room displays are not visible from public areas.
Security operations monitors badge events and video at GCCs and stations and investigates alarms.
regulatory_driver: C-ENERGY-R02 (SD 01G II.C (physical attack on network infrastructure))

implementation_statement: Visitor access records for control rooms are kept 2 years.
Power cabling for control rooms and data rooms is protected and separated.
Emergency power-off controls are guarded and limited to data rooms.
UPS and generators support both GCCs for at least 72 hours; compressor station control buildings have UPS for at least 8 hours.
Emergency lighting covers control rooms and exits.
Fire detection and clean-agent suppression protect data rooms at both GCCs.
Environmental controls in data rooms are monitored with alerts.
Water sensors are installed in data rooms at both GCCs.
Delivery of equipment to the GCCs is received and logged at the loading dock outside the control room area.
Controllers do not work remotely; no PSGCS control function is available from alternate work sites other than GCC-2.
GCC-2 is located more than 200 miles from GCC-1 to reduce shared hazards such as hurricanes.
Planning requirements are set in POL-01 and the policy hierarchy (P06).
This SSP is reviewed each year and after major changes; it is incorporated by reference into the Cybersecurity Implementation Plan (SD 02G Section IV.A).
Workforce and vendors with PSGCS access acknowledge rules of behavior (POL-05) each year.
The PSGCS security architecture defines zones by criticality and consequence (control, station, field, DMZ, business) and is described in the Cybersecurity Implementation Plan.
evidence: Zone and conduit diagram; CIP section III.B

implementation_statement: The High baseline from SP 800-53B is selected, tailored with the OT overlay in NIST SP 800-82 Rev. 3 Appendix F.
Tailoring decisions (for example, console lock and lockout deviations) are recorded with compensating controls.
Personnel security requirements are set in POL-01 and HR procedures.
Controller, SCADA engineer, and OT security positions are designated high risk.
Background checks are completed before access for high-risk positions and vendor technicians with OT access.

Termination events disable OT and IT accounts within 4 hours; shared passwords known to the person are changed (see IA-5 gap). Gap: PS-3 legacy SCADA accounts are disabled from a weekly report; 2 of 10 sampled PS-3 terminations were disabled 3 and 5 days late (POAM-016).
evidence: HR and OT workflow records; P07 PS-4 results

implementation_statement: Transfers trigger an access review within 5 business days (see AC-2 gap).
Access agreements, including SSI nondisclosure for covered persons, are signed before access.
Vendor personnel security requirements are in contracts and verified at onboarding.
Sanctions for policy violations follow PRC-01.1.
Position descriptions for controllers and OT roles include security duties and the controller authority defined under 192.631(b).
Risk assessment requirements are set in STD-01.1 (P06).
The PSGCS is categorized High (SSP section 6), approved by the COO.
The enterprise risk analysis (P01) covers the PSGCS each year and after major changes such as the PS-3 acquisition.
Supply chain risks for SCADA, station control, and telecommunications suppliers are assessed during tiering and each year.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-02 Security operations (SOC and OT monitoring cell)
implementation_statement: Passive vulnerability identification runs continuously on monitored OT networks; credentialed scans of Windows hosts run monthly in maintenance windows at the GCCs. Gap: hosts at 31 stations are not credential-scanned (POAM-020).
Risk responses are tracked in the register and POA&M.
Critical Cyber Systems and their critical components (SCADA hosts, front ends, station PLCs, remote valve RTUs) are identified through the BIA and the SD 02G Section III.A analysis.
Acquisition requirements are set in STD-01.3 (P06).
OT security funding is planned in the annual capital plan, including the station HMI replacement program.
SCADA projects follow a lifecycle with security gates (API RP 1165 sections required by 192.631(c)(1) for SCADA displays).
OT contracts since 2024 include security requirements, vulnerability disclosure, and incident notice terms (see SA-9 gap for older contracts).
Vendor administrator and security guides are kept in the SCADA engineering library.
Security engineering principles (defense in depth, least functionality, fail-safe to manual operation) are applied in SCADA designs.
External services (carriers, SCADA vendor support, compression manufacturers' monitoring) are tiered and reviewed each year. Gap: 2 of 6 critical OT suppliers lack incident notice terms (POAM-014).
The SCADA vendor's configuration management of delivered software is verified at factory acceptance testing.
Each SCADA release is tested in the SCADA test environment, including security regression tests.
The SCADA vendor's development process is reviewed in the supplier assessment.
The SCADA vendor trains company engineers on secure configuration.

control_name: Developer Security and Privacy Architecture and Design
implementation_statement: The SCADA vendor provides a security architecture description for the platform.
Vendor developers with access to company configurations are screened under contract.
Unsupported components are tracked with mitigations. Gap: 22 stations run end-of-support HMIs or PLC firmware; mitigations documented for 15 (POAM-003).
evidence: Unsupported component register; P07 SA-22 results

implementation_statement: System and communications protection is set in STD-01.5 and STD-04.1 (P06).

control_name: Separation of System and User Functionality
implementation_statement: User functions (consoles) are separated from system management functions (SCADA servers, engineering workstations).
Security functions (domain controllers, privileged access, logging) run on dedicated hosts in a separate OT management zone.
Shared resources on SCADA hosts are cleared between processes by the platform.
The SCADA network is not reachable from the internet; telecommunications use rate limits and redundant paths.
Boundaries separate control, station, field, DMZ, and business zones with firewalls at each conduit. Gap: 12 of 20 PS-3 compressor stations have flat networks (POAM-016).
External connections to the PSGCS are limited to the gateway, the DMZ replicas, and documented interconnect links.
Each external connection has a documented rule set reviewed quarterly.

control_name: Deny by Default, Allow by Exception
implementation_statement: Boundary firewalls deny by default and allow by exception.

SCADA traffic that crosses shared carrier networks is encrypted in IPsec tunnels. Gap: PS-3 polling crosses the corporate MPLS shared with business traffic without encryption (POAM-016; SD 02G Section III.B.2.b).
Network sessions for remote and engineering access end after 30 minutes idle.
Keys and certificates for the gateway, VPNs, and device certificates are managed by the OT public key infrastructure.
Cryptography uses current approved algorithms.
Not applicable: no collaborative computing devices (cameras, microphones) are part of PSGCS components; control room phones are outside the SCADA network.
The OT public key infrastructure issues certificates under a documented policy.
Mobile code (macros, scripts) is blocked on SCADA hosts and consoles by allowlisting.
Authoritative DNS for OT names is internal; no public names exist for OT systems.

control_name: Secure Name/Address Resolution Service (Recursive or Caching Resolver)
implementation_statement: OT resolvers validate responses from internal authoritative servers only.

control_name: Architecture and Provisioning for Name/Address Resolution Service
implementation_statement: OT DNS servers are redundant at both GCCs.
Session authenticity is protected by TLS on the gateway and by IPsec on telecommunications tunnels.
Station controls fail to a safe state (hold last value or safe shutdown by the hardwired emergency shutdown system) when communications are lost.
SCADA backups and configuration exports are encrypted at rest.
SCADA host operating systems isolate processes; SCADA services run under separate service accounts.
System and information integrity requirements are set in STD-01.5 and STD-01.8 Patch and Vulnerability Standard (P06).

Patches are categorized by criticality with timelines, and entries in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog are prioritized (STD-01.8). Gap: 9% of applicable Known Exploited Vulnerabilities items are past the plan's timeline, mostly at legacy stations (POAM-002).
evidence: Patch status report; P07 SI-2 results

implementation_statement: Malicious code protection runs on SCADA hosts and engineering workstations in vendor-approved modes; allowlisting protects consoles; transient devices are scanned at kiosks.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-02 Security operations (SOC and OT monitoring cell)
implementation_statement: Passive OT network monitoring at GCC-1, GCC-2, and 74 of 96 stations detects deviations from the communications baseline, new devices, and unauthorized commands. Gap: no monitoring at 22 stations (including all PS-3 stations) or at meter and valve sites (POAM-005).
evidence: Sensor coverage report; P07 SI-4 results

provider_if_inherited: CCP-02 Security operations (SOC and OT monitoring cell)
implementation_statement: Inbound and outbound traffic at the DMZs is monitored for unusual or unauthorized activity, including command-and-control and anonymization services.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-02 Security operations (SOC and OT monitoring cell)
implementation_statement: Threat intelligence from CISA, TSA, and the sector information sharing center is triaged by the OT monitoring cell.
Security function verification runs after each SCADA release and quarterly (allowlisting, logging, account policies).
File integrity monitoring runs on SCADA hosts and consoles; PLC logic is compared to the golden copy monthly. Gap: legacy stations have no automated logic comparison (POAM-003).
Planned: signed firmware and logic verification for new station PLCs in the replacement program (2027 to 2028).

provider_if_inherited: CCP-02 Security operations (SOC and OT monitoring cell)
implementation_statement: Enterprise email filtering blocks spam and phishing; no email reaches the SCADA network.
The SCADA front end validates field data ranges and protocol format and flags out-of-range values for controllers.
Error messages on consoles do not reveal system internals to unauthorized users.

responsible_role: Vice President, Pipeline Safety and Compliance
implementation_statement: PSGCS records are retained as required by 192.631(j) and the company records schedule; SSI is retained and destroyed under 49 CFR 1520.19.
SCADA hosts use vendor-supported memory protection features (data execution prevention, address randomization).
Supply chain risk management is set in STD-01.3 (P06).
The supply chain risk management plan covers SCADA, station control, telecommunications, and analytics suppliers.
Supply chain controls include supplier tiering, security terms, and acceptance testing. Gap: no software bills of materials from the SCADA vendor (POAM-014).
OT equipment is bought from the manufacturer or authorized distributors only.
Critical OT suppliers are reviewed each year. Gap: 2 of 6 critical OT suppliers have no incident notice terms (POAM-014).
Contracts since 2024 require notice of compromises and vulnerabilities (see SR-6 gap).
Planned: tamper-evident seals and enclosure intrusion switches on station PLC cabinets in the replacement program.
Planned: inspection of PLCs and RTUs for tampering at receipt and during annual maintenance, starting 2027.
Counterfeit components are prevented through authorized sourcing and acceptance testing.
Disposed OT components are sanitized or destroyed with certificates.
